paper.title: Towards a general theory of adaptive walks on rugged fitness landscapes

headline: Kauffman NK landscape (agent-based): 3/3 locked clauses REPRO; #local optima rises 1 -> 2043 as K goes 0 -> 14 (random expectation 2048); greedy-walk length falls 7.43 -> 1.58

verdicts.gate: P1 mean #local optima increases monotonically with K
P2 K=0 -> exactly 1 local optimum (single-peaked Mt-Fuji landscape)
P3 mean greedy adaptive-walk length decreases monotonically with K

extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic model; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + discipline reproduce the NK ruggedness-vs-K results (more optima, shorter adaptive walks, #optima -> 2^N/(N+1) at K=N-1) and would catch an artifact. The random-landscape expectation is the comparison anchor, never an input to the dynamics.

citations: Kauffman, S.A. & Levin, S. (1987). Towards a general theory of adaptive walks on rugged fitness landscapes. J. Theor. Biol. 128(1):11-45. doi:10.1016/S0022-5193(87)80029-2.
Kauffman, S.A. (1993). The Origins of Order: Self-Organization and Selection in Evolution. Oxford University Press (ch. 2-3: the NK model; #optima ~ 2^N/(N+1) at K=N-1; adaptive walk lengths).

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction graded against the locked ruggedness-vs-K predictions and the analytic random-landscape optima count
